messages.author: eb762f049c898baa
messages.subject: Relative amplitude not adequate shown
parts:
Hi all,
 
I got the following problem: I work with a call sequence of a frog that starts with a low and ends up with a relative high amplitude. These differences are not shown in the plot made with "oscillo" nor "spectro". I have the different calls in three wav. files and they look the same, but even if I copy them in one .wav file they don´t show any difference in amplitude (this is not so at all if opened in e.g. audacity). Any ideas how to show the "real" relative amplitude?
 
Thanks in advance!
 
cheers,
Martin

messages.author: 44c03a0165efd08f
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Relative amplitude not adequate shown
parts:
Hi Martin,

I'm not 100% sure what is going on, but I suspect that your file is being normalized before or during the pastew() function. There might be a way to stop that, but I'm not sure exactly how to. Possibly, you might consider looking at the non-normalized amplitude envelope: env(..., norm = F), but that's just a guess.

A work around would be to use the command line program "SoX" to concatenate the files together before comparing them with oscillo() or spectro().  Make sure you have Sox installed (http://sox.sourceforge.net/) and you can call it from R using the sox() function.

To concatenate (or paste together in sequence) your wave files use the following command:

sox("frog1.wav frog2.wav frog3.wav threecalls.wav")  ##this pastes them together into a new wave and saves it to the working directory
calls <- readWave("threecalls.wav")  ##Open the new wave file
oscillo(calls)

Alternatively you could combine them with Audacity, but this could be time consuming if you have a lot to do.

Good luck,

Steffi

messages.author: eb762f049c898baa
messages.subject: Aw: Re: [seewave] Relative amplitude not adequate shown
parts:
Hi Stefanie,
sorry for the delay and thanx a lot for the answer. I found out the the problem (three seperate files with very different amplitudes that appear in the graphs to have the same amplitude) is actually a ylim problem. Of course the amplitude is adequate shown for each graph, I see this when I choose the yaxt="s" option: the three graphs differ in the y-values. So, I tried to show the same y-range in every single oscillogram (using the maximum of the loudest call as upper y-limit) to make the differnces clear. However, it seems the using "ylim" on combination with "oscillo" does not work - at least I tried and played around with different c(-n, n), but it doesn´t work.
As well, I still have no good idea how to adjust the amplitudes in the spectograms. I made some adjustments with "collevels" function, but it is not what is right, I guess.
Thanks for any advice!
Cheers,
Martin

messages.subject: Re: Aw: Re: [seewave] Relative amplitude not adequate shown
parts:
Hi Martin,
You are right there is no ylim option in oscillo().
Note also tha wave object are scaled betwen -1 and 1 before to be plotted by oscillo() or spectro().
You may just plot your files manually. It is not that difficult for an oscillogram:
plot(sound@left, type="l")
HTH a bit,
Jerome
